evals.name: distill-references-into-taste
evals.prompt:
Capture my design preferences into a TASTE.md. Here are my references:

1. I love how Linear feels — dense, keyboard-first, no decoration. Everything has a reason.
2. My current app feels 'too generic AI design' — centered hero, three cards, gradient buttons. I hate that.
3. I want precision over personality. Typography should carry the brand, not decorative effects.
4. For dashboards: information hierarchy before visual drama. For landing pages: one strong visual thesis, not five competing CTAs.
5. I keep going back to Stripe's documentation — the way they use color deliberately, one accent per page, generous whitespace between sections.
6. Anti-pattern: never use purple-to-pink gradients. Never use emoji as icons. Never use glassmorphism.

Distill this into TASTE.md.

assertions.text: Output follows TASTE.md structure with Product Context, Taste Values, Anti-Patterns, Decision Rules, Critique Questions, and Execution Dials sections
Anti-Patterns section captures the user's explicit negatives: purple-to-pink gradients, emoji icons, glassmorphism
Decision Rules section includes falsifiable rules like 'one accent per page' and 'typography carries brand'
Retains user's strong phrasing (e.g. 'too generic AI design') in quotes or direct references
Positive References section names Linear, Stripe documentation as aspirational sources
Output is compact — uses bullets and short imperatives, avoids long theory paragraphs

evals.name: distill-from-feedback-and-screenshots
evals.prompt:
I've been iterating on a SaaS analytics dashboard and I keep giving the same feedback. Distill my critique into TASTE.md so I stop repeating myself:

Feedback I've given across 3 review rounds:
- 'The sidebar is too wide — it's eating 30% of the screen. Make it 240px max.'
- 'Stop using different border-radius values. Pick one: 6px. Every card, button, input gets 6px.'
- 'The data tables look like Excel. More whitespace between rows, less grid lines.'
- 'We only need two font weights: 400 for body, 600 for headings. Drop the 500 and 700.'
- 'Alerts should be a thin left-border accent, not a colored background pill.'
- 'Charts should use desaturated colors with one bright accent for the highlighted data point.'
- 'Never auto-play animations. Respect prefers-reduced-motion.'

Mode preferences:
- When I ask for a new page, show me the layout wireframe first, then build.
- When I ask for a design review, audit against TASTE.md before suggesting changes.
- When we're close to shipping, only fix P1 issues — no more polish passes.

Write TASTE.md.

assertions.text: Output follows TASTE.md structure with Product Context, Taste Values, Anti-Patterns, Decision Rules, and Execution Dials sections
Design Locks section captures explicit constraints: 240px sidebar, 6px border-radius, two font weights (400/600)
Workflow Modes section encodes the three modes: show wireframe first, audit against TASTE.md, P1-only near shipping
Decision rules are mechanical and falsifiable — e.g. 'alerts use thin left-border accent, not colored background pill'
Preflight Checks section includes prefers-reduced-motion and border-radius consistency checks
Playbooks To Load section names the relevant skills or documents for each workflow mode
